(B) Axial contrast-enhanced CT, July 2025. (C) Sagittal contrast-enhanced CT, November 2022. (D) Sagittal contrast-enhanced CT, July 2025. On the 2022 imaging (panels A and C), the hernial sac contained small bowel, transverse colon, the distal antrum/pylorus, mesenteric fat and SMA branches, with no proximal gastric dilatation and no radiological evidence of obstruction; the hernial neck measured 5.7 × 7.5 cm (transverse × cranio-caudal). On the 2025 imaging (panels B and D), the hernial neck dimensions were essentially unchanged (5.6 × 7.5 cm), but the sac now accommodated substantially more viscera: a markedly distended, fluid- and air-filled stomach occupied the central and right paraumbilical region, with the mechanical transition point at the level of the distal antrum and pylorus where the gastric outlet is extrinsically angulated as it crosses the fascial defect. The small bowel and colon distal to this transition are decompressed, in keeping with mechanical obstruction at the gastric outlet rather than at a more distal level. There is no gastric wall thickening, mass lesion or peri-gastric fat stranding to suggest an alternative malignant or inflammatory cause.
